scope: Wave 0 containment only: disabled fan-voting and dispute entry points, removal of the generic audit callable, denial of direct client writes to protected collections, strict temporary player bootstrap defaults, and legacy audit provenance labeling.
scopeLimit: This is not a whole-application or Android V1 release security score. Wave 1 trusted operations and dispute authorization, Wave 2 private/public player separation, CI, dependency, device, and release gates remain open.
summary: All Wave 0 containment controls are present in the candidate tree and their scoped attack and authentication tests pass. No Firebase deployment or Remote Config publication was performed.

evidence: fan_voting_enabled and disputes_enabled default to false
match cards hide the fan-voting entrance by default
direct fan-voting and dispute routes fail closed unless explicitly enabled
the generic callable implementation was removed
Firestore rules deny direct client create, update, and delete for auditEvents
Firestore rules deny direct vote, voting-session, and dispute writes
temporary players/{uid} creation uses an exact field allowlist and trusted bootstrap defaults
rules attacks reject forged role, rating, wins, trust level, createdAt, extra fields, and cross-UID creation
audit events require trustedOperation provenance version 1 and a non-empty requestId to be treated as trusted
events without complete provenance are labeled قديم غير موثق in the organizer timeline

fullFlutterSuite.note: Both failures expect bracket-screen-summary-bar in tournament_operations_dashboard_test.dart and are tracked by ELR-UX-302 and ELR-UX-303; no Wave 0 file caused either failure.

remainingRisks.risk: Trusted server-side audit, voting, and atomic dispute operations plus relationship-scoped reads are not implemented yet.
Private player documents are still readable more broadly than the final privacy model permits; public-profile projection and cutover remain required.
Two existing knockout-bracket widget tests remain red outside this security scope.

recommendations: Do not deploy the contained voting or dispute flows as finished features; keep both flags false until Wave 1 passes its own gate.
Implement audit creation only inside trusted backend operations and remove the temporary denied client attempt in Wave 1.
Complete the private/public player-profile cutover before claiming application-wide security readiness.
Review the Firestore rules and this scoped result before any production deployment.
releaseDecision: Wave 0 containment gate passes locally. Android V1 release remains blocked by Waves 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.
